Subject: Missing billing events / partial chunked frames (FinPay production)

Hi Grace —

We're seeing a spike in missing billing events in our reconciliation job for the 08:00–09:30 PST window. The events arrive via your realtime stream and are then forwarded into our billing pipeline. Over ~90 minutes we observed ~2.3% of events either truncated mid-JSON or not arriving at all; downstream replay shows late arrivals (several minutes) causing billing variance and duplicate counters.

Attached is a small replay sample and the pacer log. This started at ~08:05 and repeats every ~10–20 minutes. Our SRE sees many 524/504-like timeouts at the edge and chunked frames that never complete (stream goes silent). We flagged it as high-impact because our month-end invoice will be off if we can't reconcile.

Can you confirm if Redwood experienced any streaming degradation in our region this morning? We need a call ASAP — heads up: procurement may ask for credits if invoices are affected.

Liam
FinPay — Platform Engineering

Quick triage notes from SRE (initial):
- Observed transient stalls on the chunked-transfer path originating at the HTTP edge for customer FinPay across us-west-2 during 08:02–08:25.
- Pattern: initial chunk(s) delivered, then connection silence for ~15–90s before either resuming or closing with 499/504. No backend model CPU spike correlates.
- Hypothesis: proxy-level backpressure + late FIN window -> TCP keepalive/idle timeout mismatch causing socket closure without clean FIN -> client sees truncated chunked JSON.

Immediate mitigation options (recommended):
1) Temporarily route FinPay to a Dedicated low-latency pool (isolates from proxy contention) — requires ops signoff for capacity.
2) Toggle longer chunk-timeout (increase idle keepalive on their route from 30s -> 120s) as a short-term config change.
3) Offer them a short-term non-streaming fallback (batching every 10s) for critical billing topics while we root-cause.

Attaching pacer logs and packet captures from the edge; will follow with a narrower timeline and correlation graphs.

- Hannah
Head of SRE (acting), Redwood Inference
